lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: وَقَبَ is in the derivative form: وَقَبَ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
و/ق/ب   w–q–b holes in the rock where rainwater collects; foolish person; heavy drinker; to sink in, to subside; to disappear, to darken. Of this root, وَقَبَ waqaba, occurs 1 time in the Qur’an
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
وَقَبَ waqaba i [v. intrans.] to enter, to cover with darkness, to prevail

(113:3) وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ and of the evil of the dark night [also interpreted as: darkness, the moon, or the Pleiades] when it prevails.
